title: Villa Camille
area: Between Monaco and Cap Martin, facing the sea
features: Belle Époque villa built in 1891 by Camille Blanc
Unobstructed view over the sea and Monaco
Pool and three terraces in a garden of trees
Second villa of 205 m², suited to guests
short: A Belle Époque villa of 1891 above Monaco, pale stone and balustrades over an open sea.
long: Built in 1891 for Camille Blanc and drawn by the architect Schmidt, the house stands just west of Monaco with nothing between its terraces and the sea. Five levels hold two salons with marble fireplaces, a dining room, an independent garden apartment and bedrooms for a large family, the principal suite turned toward Monaco. The pool lies on a wide terrace among palms and cypress. A second villa of 205 square metres and a garage for two cars complete the estate.

title: La Pergola
area: Centre of Beaulieu, near the marina
features: Private garden in the centre of town
Principal suite with a glimpse of the sea
Walk to the marina and beaches
short: A white Belle Époque villa in the centre of Beaulieu, its garden and long pool sheltered by cypress.
long: Fully renovated and set in the very centre of Beaulieu, this Belle Époque villa keeps something rare in the town: a private garden. A marble staircase rises from the entrance hall to a double living room full of light. Upstairs, the principal suite has a quiet glimpse of the sea, with two further suites beside it, and three more bedrooms open onto the garden level. Terraces and a pergola lead down to a twenty metre pool. The marina and the beaches are a short walk away.

title: Maison du Cap
features: Three suites in the main villa
Guest house with two en suite bedrooms
short: Pale stone and white walls on Cap Martin, with an infinity pool facing the sea and the mountains.
long: On the Cap Martin peninsula, a few moments from the sea, the house has been reworked in calm materials: pale stone, white walls and warm timber ceilings. The main villa opens around a double height living room, with three suites and terraces that run out to the garden. A separate guest house holds two more suites, a sauna and a quiet room for exercise. The heated infinity pool sits within some 1,410 square metres of planted gardens, entirely private.

title: Bastide des Oliviers
area: La Sine, in the countryside below Vence
features: More than one hectare of gardens
Pool house with kitchen and lounge
Natural spring feeding pool, pond and garden
short: A stone bastide of 1751 near Vence, among old olives, lawns and a long pool fed by its own spring.
long: Built in 1751 and carefully restored, the bastide stands in more than a hectare of gardens a few minutes from the old town of Vence. Ivy climbs the stone walls, and a shaded pergola leads to the door. The house holds five bedrooms over three levels, with three further buildings for guests or staff. A heated pool of nineteen by seven metres lies beside a pool house with its own kitchen, and a natural spring feeds the pool, the pond and the garden. A tennis court sits among the olives.
